status: unresolved - run build-rootfs.sh --lock on a networked build host
note: Inputs of scripts/build-rootfs.sh. This file was written in an offline container: the snapshot timestamp, the package versions, the kernel artefact hashes, the service uid/gid and the partition size below are NOT known here and are null. `sh scripts/build-rootfs.sh --lock ...` fills them in on a networked Debian/Ubuntu build host (docs/ROOTFS-BUILD.md). Until then build-rootfs.sh refuses to produce a release input and only builds with --unlocked, which stamps its output as non-reproducible and non-release.
variant_note: mmdebstrap's name for what `debootstrap` installs by default (Essential, required and important packages). docs/INSTALL.md says the verified image was made with debootstrap; whether it used the default variant is NOT recorded anywhere in this repository - confirm against the verified image's package list (docs/ROOTFS-BUILD.md, step 2) before resolving.

packages.requested_note: The names of firmware/debian-packages.json `base` (the list docs/INSTALL.md gives for the verified image); scripts/test_rootfs.py keeps the two in step. dnsmasq-base is added only by --setup-ap. See firmware/rootfs-dependencies.json for why each is there and for packages that are NOT in the verified list.

service_user.name: nassimhub
service_user.note: Fixed numeric ids, because files on the state partition (NSHSTATE) are owned by them and the first-boot script only re-owns the directory, not its contents. They MUST equal `id -u nassimhub` / `id -g nassimhub` on devices that already hold an identity; that value is not recorded in this repository.

kernel.note: The verified kernel is not built here (firmware/upstream.lock.json names its source). The release engineer supplies the verified boot image and the matching modules archive; --lock records their SHA-256 and every later build checks them, reads the release string out of the kernel itself and refuses modules whose vermagic differs.

image.label: rootfs
image.note: uuid and hash_seed are arbitrary constants so that two builds are identical; the boot command line selects the root filesystem by LABEL or PARTUUID, never by this UUID. size_mib is the size of the stick's rootfs partition: it is not documented in this repository, so it is a required parameter (--image-size-mib, read from the device's partition table).
